high.title: Is Indonesia Really Heading Towards a Crisis Like 1998?
high.summary: Economists debate whether Indonesia is heading towards a 1998-style crisis amid rupiah weakness and market volatility. Bank Permata's Chief Economist argues Indonesia's current economic structure is much stronger than during the Asian crisis, with better banking sector health and inflation control.

high.title: Purbaya: We Are Not Heading Towards 1998, Only Negative Sentiment
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya firmly denies Indonesia is heading towards a 1997-98 style crisis, stating that fiscal fundamentals remain strong. He attributes current rupiah pressure to negative market sentiment that can be addressed through better coordination between government and Bank Indonesia.

high.title: Purbaya Reveals Root Cause of Continuous IHSG Decline: Negative Economic Perception
high.summary: Indonesia's main stock index (IHSG) has plummeted 35.30% to 5,594.76 in 2026, down from over 9,100 earlier this year. Finance Minister Purbaya attributes the decline to negative sentiment despite strong economic fundamentals and growing economic activity nationwide.

high.title: BI Governor Meets Purbaya at Parliament, Agrees on Two Strategies to Protect Rupiah Exchange Rate
high.summary: Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo emphasizes strengthened coordination between monetary and fiscal authorities to stabilize the rupiah exchange rate. The coordinated approach aims to support economic growth while defending currency stability through synchronized policy measures.

high.title: 'Sell Indonesia' Trend After Rupiah and IHSG Weakness, Purbaya Responds
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya responds to international media coverage of 'sell Indonesia' trends amid rupiah weakness and stock market decline. He argues that such coverage doesn't fully understand Indonesia's economic conditions and fundamentals remain strong.

high.title: Prabowo Signs Single Export Gateway Regulation Through SOEs: Here's the Content
high.summary: President Prabowo officially signed Government Regulation No. 24/2026 implementing single export gateway through state-owned enterprises for strategic natural resources. The policy initially covers coal, palm oil, and ferro alloys, representing a major shift in export governance structure.

high.title: KoinWorks Boss Detained by Attorney General's Office, Shareholders Summoned by OJK
high.summary: Financial Services Authority (OJK) summons KoinWorks shareholders following corruption allegations and detention of three company executives by the Attorney General's Office. The case involves suspected misuse of peer-to-peer lending operations, raising concerns about fintech oversight.

high.title: Gold Price Plunges This Deep in One Week
high.summary: Gold prices in Indonesia dropped significantly from Rp 2.799 million per gram on June 1 to Rp 2.738 million per gram on June 6, representing a substantial weekly decline. The price volatility reflects broader market uncertainties affecting precious metals trading.

medium.title: SBY's Strategy to Help Indonesia Escape the 2008 Economic Crisis
medium.summary: Former President Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono shares insights on how Indonesia survived the 2008 global financial crisis through maintaining market confidence, fiscal prudence, and strong policy coordination. His experience offers lessons for current economic challenges facing Indonesia.

medium.title: Bank Mandiri Taspen Fires Employee Suspected of Investment Fraud
medium.summary: PT Bank Mandiri Taspen terminates an employee involved in fraudulent investment schemes at its Purwokerto branch. The bank emphasizes zero tolerance for integrity violations and cooperation with law enforcement in ongoing legal proceedings.

medium.title: Djarum Group Company IBST Plans Delisting, Voluntary Tender at Rp 5,400 per Share
medium.summary: PT Inti Bangun Sejahtera Tbk (IBST), owned by Djarum Group, announces plans to delist from Indonesia Stock Exchange through voluntary tender offer at Rp 5,400 per share. The offer price exceeds previous mandatory tender and recent trading averages, targeting public shareholders.

medium.title: Indonesia Has Opportunity to Avoid US Import Tariffs
medium.summary: Indonesia has strong prospects for tariff relief from the US as USTR considers 18 product exclusion requests under Section 301 investigation. This potential relief could reduce export costs and improve competitiveness of Indonesian products in American markets.

medium.title: Indonesia to Face New 10% Tariff from US, Government Responds
medium.summary: US Trade Representative proposes 10-12.5% tariffs on imports from 60 countries including Indonesia under Section 301 investigation related to forced labor practices. The Indonesian government is studying the announcement and its potential impact on bilateral trade relations.

medium.title: Root Cause of 3,100 Containers Piling Up at Tanjung Priok Port
medium.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya investigates container congestion at Tanjung Priok Port, with 3,100 containers and 3,000 related documents delayed. The bottleneck threatens industrial supply chains and increases dwelling time, prompting direct ministerial intervention to resolve operational issues.

medium.title: Purbaya Responds to Claims that Free Nutritious Meals and Village Cooperatives Burden State Budget
medium.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya denies that flagship programs including Free Nutritious Meals and Village Cooperatives strain the state budget. He emphasizes program flexibility and President Prabowo's willingness to implement efficiency measures when needed.

medium.title: Said Iqbal on Cabinet Rumors: Just Wait
medium.summary: Indonesian Workers' Confederation (KSPI) President Said Iqbal addresses speculation about joining the cabinet, asking public to wait for official announcement from State Secretary. His potential appointment could signal greater labor representation in economic policy-making.

medium.title: Food Price Update: Cooking Oil and Onions Rise, Chili Still at Rp 75,000/kg
medium.summary: Most food prices show mixed trends with red onions rising 6.99% to Rp 54,350/kg and cooking oil prices increasing across all categories. Rice prices remain relatively stable while chili prices stay elevated at Rp 75,000/kg, affecting household purchasing power.
